topics.topic: Whether record_change operations require the record's expected lifecycle status
questions: Must AcceptBindingChange apply whatever the binding's current status is, or only when the binding is proposed?
Must DecideApprovalChange and RecordAttemptOutcomeChange apply whatever the current status is, or only to a requested approval and an in_flight attempt respectively?
Must ResolveAttemptChange, RevokeChange and RecoverInFlightChange apply whatever the current status is, or only to unknown, active and in_flight records respectively?
Must AcceptBindingChange require the binding to be proposed, or update it regardless of its current status?
Must DecideApprovalChange require the approval to be requested, or update it regardless of its current status?
Must RecordAttemptOutcomeChange require an in_flight attempt, or update the attempt regardless of its current status?
Must ResolveAttemptChange require an unknown attempt, or update the attempt regardless of its current status?
Must RevokeChange require an active grant, or update the grant regardless of its current status?
Must RecoverInFlightChange require an in_flight attempt, or update the attempt regardless of its current status?

quotes: It checks no status of the record a lifecycle change updates and sets that change's fields whatever status the record has: the status a change may start from is the caller's rule, and one request ends before the next begins (A18), so no other request can have changed it meanwhile.

ProposeBindingChange writes an OperationBinding with status proposed; AcceptBindingChange sets a proposed binding to accepted with accepted_at; ComposeFlowVersionChange writes the FlowVersion and its StoredValues, plus the Flow with created_flow_purpose as purpose when that is given; ActivateFlowVersionChange writes one FlowActivation; StartRunChange writes a Run with status running, its pinned implementations, inputs and StoredValues and no waiting points.

RequestApprovalChange writes an EffectApproval with status requested; DecideApprovalChange sets a requested approval to approved or refused per the = models.OwnerDecision value with decided_at and, for a refusal, writes its refusal_execution as the element's NodeExecution; RecordAttemptInFlightChange writes an EffectAttempt with status in_flight and the inputs the change carries; RecordAttemptOutcomeChange sets the in_flight attempt's status and concluded_at, writes its concluding NodeExecution, StoredValues and SpooledFiles and sets the approval named by used_approval_id to used.

RecordReadOutcomeChange writes the concluding NodeExecution with its StoredValues and SpooledFiles and no attempt; RecordOperationFailureChange writes one NodeExecution and no attempt; ResolveAttemptChange sets an unknown attempt's status to the AttemptStatus member named like its AttemptResolution (applied or not_applied) and its resolved_by; a resolution records no time of its own; GrantChange writes a StandingGrant with status active; RevokeChange sets an active grant to revoked with revoked_at; RecoverInFlightChange sets one in_flight attempt to unknown with concluded_at, writes its NodeExecution when given and sets used_approval_id's approval to used when given.
judgement.divergence: One implementer updates each lifecycle record regardless of its current status; another requires proposed, requested, in_flight, unknown, or active status as the variant notes state. Callers observe either an accepted update or an error/no update for the same change.
judgement.why: The general behavior rule forbids status checks, while the variant field-assignment notes describe the updates as applying to records in specific statuses.

topics.topic: Whether the module or caller assigns SpooledFile attempt_number
questions: Does the module assign the attempt_number carried by each SpooledFile record, or does the caller supply it in the file key?

Must record_change alone assign the attempt_number of a SpooledFile record inside its transaction, or must the caller supply the attempt_number used by spool_file before that transaction? Narrow “every record it writes whose model carries one” to exclude SpooledFile, or change the spool publication flow so the module assigns that number.

quotes: The module alone assigns, inside the transaction: store positions; the random identities trial_execution_id, binding_id, run_id, approval_id and grant_id, drawn from a cryptographically secure source — a run_id as secrets.token_hex of the imported STORE_RUN_ID_TOKEN_BYTES constant, the form the run spool directories are checked against — and drawn again on a collision, which is a drawn identity for which the row's load operation finds a row; the attempt_number of every record it writes whose model carries one; and every by-field (issued_by, created_by, submitted_by, added_by, activated_by, executed_by, proposed_by, accepted_by, authored_by, started_by, cancelled_by, resumed_by, released_by, decided_by, granted_by, revoked_by, resolved_by) from the actor argument; and exactly the statuses the field-assignment notes of the variants say they write or set, and no other; every other field, times included, comes from the change as given, except a field the change does not carry, which is empty until a later change sets it.

A NodeExecution whose files were spooled before it is written carries the attempt_number its caller spooled them under, the element's next number read as the count of its NodeExecutions plus one; the change is refused with RefusedError, writing nothing, when that number is no longer the element's next, and no caller ever chooses another number.
The attempt_number of file is the element's next number as the caller read it; spool_file assigns none.
judgement.divergence: One implementer replaces or assigns each SpooledFile attempt_number inside record_change; another preserves the caller-supplied attempt_number already used to publish the file. The caller and subsequent spool lookup observe whether the recorded key still identifies the published file.
judgement.why: SpooledFile carries attempt_number and is written by record_change, so the universal module-assignment rule conflicts with the explicit caller-assignment and spool_file-assignment rules.

topics.topic: Whether open_store removes spool temporary files
questions: Must open_store remove spool temporary files through remove_spool_temporaries, or must no spool be removed by this call?

quotes: last, call remove_spool_temporaries for data_directory, which creates the spool area when absent and removes the temporaries of an interrupted spool publish, re-raising its SpoolInternalError as StoreInternalError.

Returns StoreOpened with data_directory and temporary_files_removed, the count of temporary files removed from the content-addressed area plus the count remove_spool_temporaries returns, unnamed value files not counted; no record, named value file or spool is removed by this call; the spools of ended runs are removed later in the start sequence, by run recovery (A18 rule 4).
judgement.why: The text expressly requires removal of interrupted-publish temporaries while separately preserving completed spools.
